correctness.rationale: The proof covers exact quantifiers m,n>=2: S dominates iff incidence graph has no simultaneously isolated row and column, and L(B_S) has perfect matching iff every edge-bearing component has even edge count; the latter is constructively proved by even-indegree orientation. Exponential formula and formal sign filtering yield the stated generating function, with inclusion-exclusion for domination. Minimum-size lower/upper bounds and all parity/square leading counts are checked casewise. Independent direct matching, formal-series, and occupancy programs agree on all tested coefficients and ten leading counts. Computations supplement rather than substitute for the general proof.

originality.rationale: The all-coefficient paired-domination polynomial for arbitrary rectangular rook graphs and its parity-sensitive minimum multiplicities were not found in the inspected primary results or relevant public research-record comparisons. Ordinary domination, general paired-domination inequalities and paired polynomials on other graph classes do not logically imply this formula. The basic line-graph matching lemma and labelled exponential formula are recognized prior tools, not claimed independently new. Priority remains qualified by unavailable historical full texts.

Unindexed historical tables or equivalent component-parity enumerations may exist.

value.rationale: A complete coefficient formula for paired domination of the canonical rook-graph family is a motivated exact graph invariant with a nontrivial matching restriction. It recovers all feasible cardinality counts, isolates an interpretable even-component structural obstruction and determines leading counts including parity- and square-boundary phases. Ordinary domination polynomials and general paired minimum inequalities do not give these enumerations; no downstream theorem or asymptotic result is claimed.
